rationale: bugs_open/303: every truncation guard on component HTML decides 'was this generation cut?' by raw substring counting — strings.Count(folded, "<script") > strings.Count(folded, "</script>") and the same for <style/<section/<div/<fieldset — with no awareness of string literals, regexes, comments or prose. A tool that MANIPULATES HTML necessarily mentions those tags in its own JavaScript, so one unpaired mention (a comment '// protect <style> blocks', a regex /<script[^>]*>/) is refused at birth, permanently, as 'truncated' — while the guard's own recorded context says ends_cleanly:true and llm_call_log shows output_tokens 13,979 of max 32,000. Both live HTML-manipulating tools passed by EXACTLY ZERO margin (surviving on a lucky regex alternation-group phrasing). A repo census (grep for the counting idiom) found SIX surfaces, five sharing the defect: toolTemplateValid (tool birth AND load — a failing tool is silently dropped from the schemas map so it can never re-render), hasUnbalancedStructuralTags (section birth), componentRegressionIssues check 2 (rewrite gate — fires exactly when a FIX adds a legitimate mention), discovery check_truncated_component (sweep + verifier + intact-version probe; the verifier can refuse to resolve an item for ever), and check_tool_completeness (advisory, tool-recreation flow, additionally case-SENSITIVE today). The fix: one shared markup-context scanner in platform/content (a leaf package importable by both actions and discovery_checks, which also retires the hand-maintained mirror of the pair list that existed only because of the import cycle). The scanner counts a token only when tag-shaped (name followed by whitespace/'>'/'/') and in markup context: comment bodies skipped, script/style raw-text bodies skipped up to the first case-insensitive close token — exactly where a browser ends the element, so every true positive is kept (a cut mid-JavaScript leaves <script with no </script anywhere after it). Recalibrated 2026-08-18 over the full live population per component_write_guard.go's standing instruction: component_versions 264 rows — 26 flagged by BOTH predicates, 0 flips; comparative check-2 over all 121 consecutive version pairs — 1 block under both (the bugs_open/012 write), 0 disagreements; content_components 300 rows — new flags a strict SUBSET (8 of old 11; zero new positives), and the 3 un-flagged rows were each hand-read: all are mentions inside CSS comments, and TWO of them carry open truncated_component work items filed as false alarms by the substring count (91007600 info-card-grid 'intact v1 available to restore' — restoring would have replaced a GOOD template; 6e2c9ebf gauntlet-round-record 'needs regeneration' — regenerating risks fabrication per bugs_open/020). The bug's verification recipe on the real stored minifier/svg-optimizer templates: as stored both pass; with the mention comment injected old refuses (the bug), new passes; truncated at 60% BOTH refuse. Error honesty (bug fix candidates 3+4): the birth refusal now states the MEASURED signals (per-pair markup-context counts, ends_cleanly, tail) instead of asserting 'the generation was cut', a claim its own payload disproved; error_code tool_birth_truncation_blocked is KEPT (queried by name in LANDMINES/bug files). No shared guarantee changes; this narrows what an existing guard refuses (a precision fix), so per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 §1 it is not architecture-scope.
